name: Computer Networks
topics: Network Basics: Topologies, Classification and Addresses
For n devices, find the number of cable links needed for mesh, ring and star topologies; classify networks by geography.
Differentiate between port, logical and physical addresses with an example; differentiate intranet, extranet and internet.
OSI and TCP/IP Reference Models
Draw the OSI reference model and explain the functions of every layer.
Compare and contrast the ISO-OSI and TCP/IP models; state the purpose of layering.
Transmission Media and Fibre Optics
Explain the principle of fibre-optic communication and light propagation through optical fibre, with its advantages.
Explain guided media (STP, UTP, coaxial) and the types of unguided media.
Error Detection and Correction: CRC, Parity, LDPC
Given the data word and divisor, find the CRC and the transmitted codeword.
Explain CRC, LRC and VRC with examples; what are LDPC codes?
Flow Control: Stop-and-Wait, Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat
Explain the sliding window protocol using Go-Back-N with an example; why move from Stop-and-Wait ARQ to Go-Back-N?
For the given timeouts in selective repeat, find the contents of the sender's window; explain piggybacking.
Medium Access Control: ALOHA, CSMA/CD, LAN Standards
Terminals share a 9600 bps channel with 200-bit frames; estimate the number of terminals supported by pure and slotted ALOHA at maximum throughput.
What is CSMA? Explain the persistence methods and the CSMA/CD protocol in Ethernet; compare Token Bus and Token Ring.
IP Addressing, Subnetting, CIDR and NAT
An organisation is granted the block 130.86.0.0/16 and wants 1024 subnets. Find the subnet mask, addresses per subnet, and first/last addresses of the first and last subnets.
Find the network address, broadcast address and subnet mask for the given host; explain CIDR notation and NAT.
IPv4 vs IPv6 Headers
Compare and contrast the IPv4 header with the IPv6 header. Why is IPv6 needed?
Routing Algorithms: Dijkstra, Link State, Distance Vector, OSPF
Use Dijkstra's algorithm to find the shortest path tree from the given node.
Compare link state and distance vector routing; explain OSPF and the advantages/disadvantages of flooding.
Transport Layer: TCP, UDP and Congestion Control
Explain TCP's three-way handshake with diagrams; draw and explain the fields of the UDP header (decode the given hex header).
Explain the leaky bucket algorithm for traffic shaping.
Application Layer: HTTP, SMTP and E-mail
Discuss the features of HTTP and how it works.
Explain the working of electronic mail and how SMTP is used.
